prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1242; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports neck strain and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss. No issues with the policy have been identified.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Independent confirmation of occupancy has been received.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the claim. They confirm several details of the impact, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision itself.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant, who described the crash consistently with the account given at first notice. The same account was repeated in every conversation so far.

Entry 6: Inspected the vehicle damage. The damage is mostly consistent with the described impact pattern and the point of contact on the side of the vehicle.

Entry 7: Searched prior claim records and inspected the vehicle for signs of earlier repairs. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 8: Received the medical summary from the treating provider. The reported neck strain is a plausible injury for a collision of this type.

Entry 9: Reviewed the claimant's medical history as disclosed. A small strain in the same area was documented years ago and resolved fully with no ongoing complaints.

Entry 10: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a neck strain of this kind. Requested updated records and a current treatment plan from the provider through counsel.

Entry 11: Discussed the file with the supervisor. The injury and vehicle damage findings are consistent with the loss as reported, and the remaining review is focused on the length of treatment.

Entry 12: Sent a status letter to claimant's counsel listing outstanding medical records and requesting the treatment timeline. File remains open pending receipt.
